description: Virtualization, kernels, protection, DMA, real-time systems and multiprocessors.

questions.optionA: Software/firmware that manages virtual machines
questions.explanation: A hypervisor provides and manages virtual machine environments.

questions.questionText: Which virtualization type runs directly on hardware?
questions.optionA: Type 1 hypervisor
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on physical hardware.

questions.questionText: Which virtualization type normally runs on a host operating system?
questions.optionA: Type 2 hypervisor
questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors run as applications on a host OS.

questions.optionA: Creating virtual versions of computing resources
questions.explanation: Virtualization abstracts physical resources into virtual environments.

questions.optionA: An isolated user-space environment sharing the host kernel
questions.explanation: Containers isolate applications while generally sharing the host OS kernel.

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between VMs and containers?
questions.optionA: VMs generally virtualize complete machines; containers share the host kernel
questions.optionC: Containers require a separate kernel each
questions.explanation: Virtual machines emulate/virtualize complete machine environments, while containers share the host kernel.

questions.optionA: Set of resources and operations accessible to a process/user
questions.explanation: A protection domain defines accessible objects and allowed operations.

questions.optionA: Restricting who can perform operations on resources
questions.explanation: Access control determines which subjects can perform which operations.

questions.optionA: Obtaining higher privileges than authorized
questions.explanation: Privilege escalation occurs when an entity gains unauthorized higher-level permissions.

questions.questionText: What is a trusted computing base?
questions.optionA: Components responsible for enforcing security policies
questions.explanation: The trusted computing base contains components relied upon for security enforcement.

questions.optionA: Kernel design keeping only essential services in kernel space
questions.explanation: Microkernels minimize kernel-resident functionality.

questions.questionText: Which services may run outside the microkernel?
questions.optionA: Device drivers and system services
questions.explanation: Microkernel designs often move drivers and services into user space.

questions.optionA: Kernel design with many OS services running in kernel space
questions.explanation: Monolithic kernels keep many core OS services in kernel space.

questions.optionA: Design combining aspects of monolithic and microkernel approaches
questions.explanation: Hybrid kernels combine architectural ideas from both approaches.

questions.optionA: Direct Memory Access
questions.explanation: DMA allows devices to transfer data to/from memory with limited CPU intervention.

questions.questionText: DMA can improve I/O performance by:
questions.optionA: Reducing CPU involvement in data transfers
questions.explanation: DMA transfers data between devices and memory with less CPU involvement.

questions.optionA: Temporary storage used during data transfer
questions.explanation: Buffers temporarily hold data while it moves between components with different speeds.

questions.optionA: Keeping frequently used data in faster storage
questions.explanation: Caching stores frequently accessed information in faster storage.

questions.questionText: What is a system call interface?
questions.optionA: Interface between user programs and OS kernel services
questions.explanation: The system call interface provides controlled access to kernel services.

questions.optionA: A family of standards for Unix-like operating systems
questions.explanation: POSIX specifies interfaces and behavior for portable Unix-like software.

questions.questionText: Which scheduling concern is important in real-time systems?
questions.optionA: Meeting timing deadlines
questions.explanation: Real-time scheduling focuses on meeting timing constraints.

questions.optionA: Critical deadlines to be met reliably
questions.explanation: Hard real-time systems have strict deadline requirements.

questions.optionA: Prefer meeting deadlines but occasional misses may be tolerated
questions.explanation: Soft real-time systems tolerate occasional timing misses with degraded quality.

questions.questionText: What is load balancing in multiprocessor systems?
questions.optionA: Distributing work among processors
questions.explanation: Load balancing attempts to distribute work so processors are utilized effectively.

questions.questionText: What is an OS protection mechanism primarily intended to prevent?
questions.optionA: Unauthorized resource access
questions.explanation: Protection mechanisms restrict unauthorized access to system resources.
